posts.title: CSAFP Just Admitted What Everyone Already Knew: The Top Was Completely MIA [Missing In Action]
posts.content:
The Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Philippines finally said it out loud. They were gone. Not on official business. Not leading from the front. Just gone. And their excuse? Demotivation. Personal issues. Distractions. That's it. That's the official reason the highest-ranking military officer in the AFP checked out and left the entire AFP to fend for itself.

Let's be clear about what this admission means. The person running the Armed Forces of the Philippines stood in front of everyone and said they couldn't be bothered to show up. Not because they were sick. Not because they were on a critical mission. Because they simply lost the drive to do their job. And nobody stopped them. Nobody held them accountable. The entire military just accepted that its leader was absent indefinitely while everything slowly fell apart.

The Branch Commanders General deserve credit for keeping things running, but let's not pretend that makes this okay. You don't get a medal for doing your job while your boss disappears. That's the bare minimum. The fact that this acknowledgment even happened tells you how bad things have gotten. When the top guy has to admit he almost quit entirely, you're way past normal problems.

Now suddenly there's this "Combat Aspects" pivot and "Medal Revision" initiative. Convenient, isn't it? After day/Months of neglect, the CSAFP suddenly discovered that awards were being handed out based on who you knew at HQ rather than what you actually accomplished. This isn't reform. This is damage control. They're trying to look like they're fixing something while the same people who created the problem pretend to be the solution.

Here's the part that really stings. The same leadership that abandoned its post now wants everyone else to show "discipline and consistency." Really? The GHQ staff is supposed to maintain standards while the highest-ranking officer admits he was checked out? That's a complete reversal of how leadership works. You don't demand excellence from others when you've demonstrated nothing but absence yourself.

The AFP didn't stagnate because junior officers stopped caring. It stagnated because nobody was steering the ship. The top was empty, and an organization cannot function without leadership at the top. Period. Now the people who were left holding the bag are expected to somehow fix everything while the same broken leadership pretends to have solutions.

This isn't a new beginning. This is the same people trying to clean up their own mess without ever admitting they made it in the first place. we are pointing to all HQ not just 1/2/3/4, But to all who neglect their responsibilities, Eating and pumping their tummy lol.
posts.author: Agent - 1

posts.title: BLACKLISTED NOON, HQ AT STAFF NA NGAYON?
posts.content:
Can we now think of the Blacklist as more of a joke than anything else? We’ve recently seen really alarming numbers of people who were recently blacklisted being allowed to work for HQ (Headquarters) and on various staff teams.
This isn’t just about a few names, but about how the message is received around the community as a whole. To take someone who has been identified as a potential threat or rule violator and give them a Staff tag establishes to every loyal participant that following the rules means nothing, and that the whole disciplinary system is a revolving door.

We are asking our current leaders directly:
What has the process been for verifying people? How can someone go from being deemed "unfit for the community" to "managing the community" with no public explanation of how their rehabilitation process works?
Security Risk: The people in those roles have access to significant amounts of power and access to the organization. Are we really going to give someone who has demonstrated an inability to follow our rules or to be trusted with our property a tool to enable them to manage them?
Morale: It is almost impossible to respect a staff team that contains members of its staff that had been openly criticized in the very recent past.

If a blacklist can be ignored this easily, then the rules don't actually exist. We need an explanation for why these individuals were fast-tracked into leadership despite their history. The community is watching, and right now, the credibility of the AFP Staff is at an all time low.
posts.author: Agent - 1

posts.title: ASC Inefficiency: Why Maintain a Server You Refuse to Use?
posts.content:
All members of the Army have been consistently frustrated with Army Supreme Command's (ASC's) inability to properly communicate to their organization, specifically with the continual use of the AFP Announcement channel for matters that are meant to be communicated internally to the Army organization itself. This leads to the question of why the Army needs to have the Army Branch Server when their Organizational Leaders do not have the Organizational Discipline to utilize it correctly.

The AFP Announcement channel exists solely for the purpose of providing Force-Wide, Mission-Critical communications. The ASC is not only creating "noise" in a senior command-level channel by using the channel for Army-specific communications but they are also demonstrating Lack of Professionalism by doing so. This does not demonstrate authority to the other services; however, it does demonstrate a need for attention and also reflects a lack of respect for the other branches' electronic infrastructure. If the ASC desires to be recognized as a "Supreme Command," they need to begin to demonstrate that they are capable of controlling their own server's activity, and not trying to "poach" from the entire AFP's visibility by using the AFP Announcement channel.
posts.author: Agent - 1

posts.title: ASC LEADING THE AFP-WIDE ACTIVITY?
posts.content: The mood within the Armed Forces of the Philippines has shifted from curiosity to deep resentment about the Army Supreme Command’s constant interference in AFP-wide activities. By consistently taking charge of joint responsibilities, the Army has pushed the AFP Supreme Command into a position of perceived inactivity. This situation leaves personnel questioning whether central leadership has been completely overlooked. This issue goes beyond a simple logistical overlap; it represents a systemic sidelining that forces the Navy and Air Force to watch their own members manipulated by a leadership that does not wear their uniform or grasp their specific operational needs. Being a Supreme Commander of a specific branch today often feels empty. It’s a title that has become a "paper authority," regularly overridden not by the General Headquarters, but by the Army’s far-reaching influence. This power imbalance creates a toxic hierarchy where branch-specific knowledge is ignored in favor of Army control, making the other branches feel like secondary parts of a joint force rather than equal partners. The key question is whether the AFP Supreme Command truly lacks the ability to lead or if the Army Supreme Command has simply decided that no one else is fit to take charge.
posts.author: Sentinel

posts.title: ANALYSIS OF THE CONFLICTING RULINGS ON MGEN BAESIC321?
posts.content:
The recent conflicting directives regarding Major General Baesic321 have raised serious concerns about the stability and coordination of the AFP leadership. While Supreme Command initially issued a wide-blacklist citing "desertion" and a "loss of confidence," the Judge Advocate General (JAG) nullified these actions minutes later, revealing that the decision was based on erroneous information and that the MGEN had actually been kicked rather than having deserted. This public contradiction suggests a significant breakdown in communication between high-ranking branches, as a "permanent" administrative ban was almost immediately overturned by a judicial finding that the individual was denied his right to a proper trial.

In light of this, we must formally ask: Does the Supreme Command actually verify evidence before issuing career-ending blacklists, or are they making these decisions without a full understanding of the facts? If the JAG confirms that the information provided to leadership was false and that judicial procedures were bypassed, it raises the question of whether the Supreme Command truly knows what they are doing or if they are acting on impulse. The AFP cannot claim to uphold the "pillars of integrity" when its own administrative and judicial branches are in such visible and unprofessional conflict.
posts.author: ANONYMOUS

posts.title: The Army Supreme Command's failure to centralize all important documents and providing a clear cohesive rules and regulations for the entirety of the Armed Forces of the Philippines.
posts.content: Adding to the ASC's outdated regulations, their negligence caused the mass confusion of the entirety of the AFP, primarily regarding which admin commands to use, which inspection procedure to follow, and so on and so forth. This lack of consistency leads to inconsistent and ineffective execution of procedures, causing frustration and unnecessary headaches for its staff and high-ranking officials.
posts.author: Zilu

posts.title: MGEN SUSPENDED FOR SUBMITTING PROPOSAL/SUGGESTION?
posts.content: A Major General of the Armored Division under the Filipino Army branch has been suspended for proposing a new method to increase the popularity of the Sergeant Major and strengthen connections between Commissioned Officers (COs) and Non-Commissioned Officers (NCOs). Despite the intent of the proposal, the Major General received a response from Supreme Command in the form of an immediate suspension from his position as Commanding Officer of the Armored Division.
posts.author: ANONYMOUS

posts.title: REPORT ON SYSTEMIC DOCUMENTATION FAILURE AND COMMAND UNRESPONSIVENESS!
posts.content: It has come to our attention that the AFP Server Information Documents still contain outdated materials produced by the previous Supreme Command, despite several months having passed since those individuals either resigned or were relieved of their duties. The current AFP Supreme Command (SP) has failed to update this information, demonstrating a significant lack of responsiveness to urgent administrative matters. Furthermore, the Admin Commands Guide is currently empty because the previous owner deleted the contents after high-ranking officials consistently ignored the protocols while the lower sections were the only ones following them. This failure to maintain and enforce updated documentation has created an operational vacuum that undermines the discipline and efficiency of the entire AFP.
